pages.text: "Me first!" Sharp-eared deer Mumu grabbed the bucket a grown-up had filled and left on the well's edge. Mumu tipped it and poured water into their own container.
"Let's fill up and go to the shore!" Quick-handed monkey Taro set down his empty container. Mumu grabbed the bucket first again. "I'm fast, so I'll pour!" Only Mumu's container held sloshing water.
Mumu grabbed it first again and again. Taro could still see the bottom of his container. Shadows grew shorter. Soon it would be everyone's rest time.
"Mumu." Taro showed his empty container. "If you always pour first, when will mine fill?" Mumu looked from one container to the other: one full, one empty.
"One bucket, but two containers." Taro pushed the bucket toward Mumu. "Your Turn, Then Mine!" Mumu turned their ears. "Then both will fill!"
Mumu tipped the bucket, pouring into their container until it was half full. Then it was Taro's turn. Mumu let go and stepped back. "Your Turn, Then Mine!"
Taking turns, they poured into this container, then that one. Both filled equally. "Look, yours is full, too!" Taro smiled.
The full containers stood together. Each friend picked up one. Taking turns had given their arms rests, too. "Doing it together is easier!" Mumu said.

With a container in one hand and the other cupped by their mouth, Mumu called, "One, pour into one container and step back! Two, your turn next! Three, when we're done, start again! Your Turn, Then Mine!"
Taro buried his face against Mumu's neck. Sharing turns filled both containers. Mumu laughed. "Both jugs are heavy now! Your Turn, Then Mine!"
